story_assessments.story_title: Europe has stretched the AI compliance clock
story_assessments.target_audience: Freelancers and solo operators who build or buy AI tools in Europe
story_assessments.audience_problem_or_desire: They want more time to experiment without missing a required review, disclosure or logging step
story_assessments.interest_signal: The deadline moved, but the rules did not disappear
story_assessments.stop_reason: It is easy to misread this as a free pass instead of a timing shift
story_assessments.promised_payoff: Understand what changed and what still needs checking before release
story_assessments.proof_point: European Commission says the AI Omnibus entered into force on 27 July 2026 and extends timelines, expands testing opportunities and reduces some administrative burdens
story_assessments.score_reason: Useful and timely for Europe-based builders, but the main value is timing and process rather than an obvious day-to-day pain point for all AI users.
story_assessments.release_gate_reason: This is mainly about compliance timing and paperwork relief, not a direct unchecked-output or pre-send review problem.

story_assessments.story_title: Google is treating AI transparency as a distribution problem
story_assessments.target_audience: Freelancers, creators and solo operators who publish client work or public content with AI help
story_assessments.audience_problem_or_desire: They want to know whether AI labels and origin signals survive when a file leaves the tool and goes to a client or platform
story_assessments.interest_signal: Transparency is becoming part of the product, not just a policy promise
story_assessments.stop_reason: The practical risk is assuming a label or disclosure exists when it may not travel with the file
story_assessments.promised_payoff: Show the simple check to make before publishing or handing off work
story_assessments.proof_point: Google said it is signing the EU AI Act transparency code and tying that to SynthID and C2PA work
search_phrases: Google EU AI Act transparency code
how to check AI content disclosure
story_assessments.score_reason: Strong practical search topic for people who publish work and need a simple pre-publication check, with a clear, ordinary-language payoff.
story_assessments.release_gate_reason: The verified evidence concerns whether AI-made or AI-edited content can be identified and whether that label survives export, which is directly tied to release checks before publication.

story_assessments.story_title: Meta is pushing AI from drafting into doing
story_assessments.target_audience: Freelancers and solo operators who use AI to help create work that clients or the public will see
story_assessments.audience_problem_or_desire: They want the convenience of AI automation without letting it send or assemble something without a fresh human check
story_assessments.interest_signal: The tool is moving from chat to task completion
story_assessments.stop_reason: Once the assistant can connect to other apps, the question becomes what it can do without approval
story_assessments.promised_payoff: Explain the new risk and the one approval check to keep in place
story_assessments.proof_point: Meta said Meta AI can make plans, connect to email and calendar apps, create slides and handle tasks on a user’s behalf
search_phrases: AI assistant can act on behalf
story_assessments.score_reason: The clearest story for a novice audience because it turns a product change into one simple, useful safeguard before anything leaves the draft.
story_assessments.release_gate_reason: The verified evidence shows an AI tool moving into actions that can affect other apps and people, which creates a direct pre-send approval problem.

story_assessments.story_title: The workplace story is not mass replacement; it is unapproved use and role redesign
story_assessments.target_audience: Freelancers and solo operators who use AI in client-facing or public work
story_assessments.audience_problem_or_desire: They want to avoid quiet, unapproved AI use slipping into real work and need one simple rule for review
story_assessments.interest_signal: A lot of people are already using AI tools their organisation never approved
story_assessments.stop_reason: The key risk is not just adoption speed but the missing approval step around it
story_assessments.promised_payoff: Give a plain-language rule that protects client work from untracked AI output
story_assessments.proof_point: Thomson Reuters said 35% of professionals see AI strategy affecting daily roles and one in three are using AI that was not officially approved
search_phrases: Thomson Reuters Future of Professionals Report 2026
story_assessments.score_reason: Very useful for workplace habits and team rules, with a straightforward message about approvals and review before output leaves the draft stage.
story_assessments.release_gate_reason: The verified evidence highlights unapproved AI use in real work, which maps directly to missing handoff and human approval before external output.

tiktok.story_title: Meta is pushing AI from drafting into doing
tiktok.target_audience: Freelancers and solo operators who use AI to help create work that clients or the public will see
tiktok.opening: Meta says its assistant can work with email and calendar.
tiktok.payoff: Keep it drafting only, and make one human check before anything sends.
tiktok.selection_reason: This is the fastest short-form hook because it names a familiar tool, shows the consequence and gives one immediate check in plain language.

youtube.story_title: Meta is pushing AI from drafting into doing
youtube.target_audience: Freelancers and solo operators who use AI to help create work that clients or the public will see
youtube.opening: Meta says its assistant can now work with email, calendar and slides, so this is no longer just a writing tool.
youtube.payoff: Check that it stays in draft mode until you approve it, then keep that human yes step for client work this week.
youtube.selection_reason: Best fit for a slightly fuller explanation because it can show the shift from drafting to acting and end with a practical next step.

facebook.story_title: The workplace story is not mass replacement; it is unapproved use and role redesign
facebook.target_audience: Freelancers and solo operators who use AI in client-facing or public work
facebook.opening: One useful number from Thomson Reuters: one in three professionals say they are using AI tools their workplace never officially approved.
facebook.payoff: The simplest safeguard is still the best one: before anything goes out, have a person check the source, the claim and the wording.
facebook.selection_reason: This sounds natural on Facebook because it reads like a practical reminder from one person to another, not a report or a policy note.

pinterest.story_title: Google is treating AI transparency as a distribution problem
pinterest.target_audience: Freelancers, creators and solo operators who publish client work or public content with AI help
pinterest.opening: If you publish client work with AI help, check one thing first.
pinterest.payoff: Ask whether the AI label still shows after export before you send or publish the file.
pinterest.selection_reason: This is the strongest Pinterest fit because people can search it as a practical how-to and save it for later use.

linkedin.story_title: The workplace story is not mass replacement; it is unapproved use and role redesign
linkedin.target_audience: Freelancers and solo operators who use AI in client-facing or public work
linkedin.opening: A third of professionals are already using AI tools their workplace never approved.
linkedin.payoff: If AI helps draft client-facing work, nothing should go out until a person checks the source, the claim and the wording.
linkedin.selection_reason: This is the cleanest LinkedIn angle because it turns a survey finding into an operational rule for teams and solo operators alike.

overall_reasoning: The strongest audience fit comes from turning the weekend stories into one simple action readers can use immediately. Story 2 is the clearest short-form TikTok and YouTube fit because it shows the shift from drafting to acting and gives a plain pre-send check. Story 1 is the best Pinterest fit because it is searchable and practical for people who publish work with AI help. Story 3 is the strongest workplace lesson for Facebook and LinkedIn because it frames the real risk as unapproved use and missing approval steps. Story 0 is useful but less specific for a novice audience than the other three. Across the set, the safest public lesson is consistent: when AI can do the next step, keep one human check before anything leaves the draft.
